papers.title: ATVHUNTER: Reliable Version Detection of Third-Party Libraries for Vulnerability Identification in Android Applications
papers.detection_method: Two-phase detection: coarse-grained CFG feature matching to filter candidates, followed by fine-grained opcode sequence matching with fuzzy rolling hash in each basic block
papers.module_decoupling: Call Dependency Graph (CDG) construction to separate library code from app code at method-level granularity
features_used: feature weighting for unique vs boilerplate code
papers.matching_algorithm: Two-stage filter-and-verify: (1) CFG similarity search to prune non-candidate libraries; (2) fuzzy rolling hash on opcode sequences for precise version matching
papers.obfuscation_handling: CDG resilient to RN and PF. Feature weighting reduces boilerplate noise. Tested on RN+PF (99.3% detection), DCR (−24%), DashO tested (partial R8 resilience)
papers.r8_resilience: Not explicitly tested on R8. DashO tested as proxy. MI (method inlining) not tested.
papers.speed: ~66s per app (benefits from two-stage filter avoiding full DB scan)
papers.dataset_size: 104,446 apps analyzed; Vulnerability DB: 1,180 CVEs from 957 TPLs (38,243 vulnerable versions), 224 security bugs from 152 TPLs (4,533 affected versions); Large-scale: 189,545 TPLs with 3,006,676 versions
papers.partial_lib_handling: Binary per library (version-level match). Partial inclusion handled implicitly via CDG module boundary detection.
papers.sbom_output: Partial — produces CVE-linked version list, no standard SBOM format
papers.cve_mapping: Yes — built-in vulnerability DB with 1,180 CVEs mapped to specific library versions
strengths: First tool combining CDG module decoupling with version-level identification and CVE mapping in a single pipeline
Two-stage architecture is highly efficient (~66s/app) by avoiding full DB scan
Large-scale empirical validation on 104K apps demonstrating real-world vulnerability prevalence
Feature weighting mechanism filters out boilerplate/common code that causes false matches
weaknesses: Not explicitly tested on R8-obfuscated apps (only DashO as proxy)
MI (method inlining) obfuscation not tested — this is the primary R8 optimization
No standard SBOM format output — just a CVE-linked version list
Transitive dependency resolution not addressed
papers.impact_on_project: High impact. ATVHUNTER's two-stage coarse-to-fine architecture (CFG filter → opcode hash verify) is directly applicable as the detection pipeline design. Its CDG-based module decoupling approach is the foundation for separating library code from app code in compiled APKs. The vulnerability DB construction methodology (1,180 CVEs across 957 libraries) provides a template for building our own CVE mapping database. The 66s per app speed demonstrates that accuracy and efficiency are compatible. Key gap to address: R8/MI resilience and standard SBOM format output.

papers.title: Version-level Third-Party Library Detection in Android Applications via Class Structural Similarity
papers.detection_method: CDG construction → neighbor feature aggregation → stateful vs stateless class splitting with Field Operation Sequence (FOS) for stateful classes and opcode similarity for stateless classes; literal feature tie-breaking for adjacent versions
papers.module_decoupling: CDG-based module decoupling at class granularity with neighbor feature aggregation — most granular approach among reviewed tools
features_used: Field Operation Sequence (FOS) for stateful classes
papers.matching_algorithm: Stateful/stateless class splitting with FOS similarity scoring + opcode similarity. Literal feature matching as tie-breaker for adjacent versions.
papers.obfuscation_handling: CDG resilient to RN, PF, CFR, DCR. Weaker on MI (method inlining/R8-opt: −10pp performance drop)
papers.r8_resilience: MI tested explicitly: −10 percentage points under method inlining (R8 optimization). Partial resilience.
papers.precision: Not explicitly reported per standard metrics, but F1 reported as harmonic mean at each level
papers.recall: Not explicitly reported per standard metrics
papers.partial_lib_handling: Per-class confidence scores — handles partial library inclusion via class-level matching granularity
papers.sbom_output: No standard SBOM format — outputs version labels only
papers.open_source: Not open source at submission time
strengths: Stateful/stateless class distinction is novel — FOS captures behavioral essence of library classes
CDG + neighbor aggregation achieves most granular module decoupling among all reviewed tools
Highest library-level F1 (97.64%) of all tools surveyed
+10.98% version-level F1 improvement over prior state-of-the-art (LIBLOOM)
weaknesses: Version-level F1 at 84.82% still leaves ~15% false rate — insufficient for production SBOM generation
MI (method inlining) causes −10pp drop — R8 resilience is incomplete
Not open source — cannot be directly used or extended
No CVE mapping or SBOM output — only version labels
papers.impact_on_project: High impact as reference benchmark. SAD's 84.82% version-level F1 is the current SOTA metric to beat for our MVP. The stateful/stateless class splitting approach (Field Operation Sequence for behavioral similarity) is directly applicable to our multi-scale fusion architecture. The CDG neighbor aggregation technique provides the most granular module decoupling pattern available. Key lessons: (1) class-level confidence scores enable partial library inclusion detection; (2) MI resilience remains the critical gap we must solve; (3) the approach validates that CDG-based methods outperform package-structure-based methods for obfuscated APKs.

papers.title: Obfuscation-resilient Detection of Android Third-Party Libraries Using Multi-Scale Code Dependency Fusion
papers.detection_method: Multi-scale fusion of three dependency graphs: class dependency, function call, and basic block dependency. Constructs Library Dependency Graph (LDG). Bayesian probability scoring for version disambiguation. Explicit SBOM generation pipeline.
papers.module_decoupling: Multi-scale CDG fusion (3-level dependency graph) — most robust approach among all reviewed tools. Class-level, method-level, and basic-block-level graphs fused.
papers.matching_algorithm: Multi-scale graph fusion → similarity scoring across 3 dependency levels → Bayesian probability for adjacent-version disambiguation → SBOM output
papers.obfuscation_handling: Designed specifically for R8 resilience. Multi-scale fusion provides redundancy — when one scale is obfuscated (e.g., basic blocks inlined), other scales (class deps, method calls) remain stable. Coverage: RN, PF, CFR, MI.
papers.r8_resilience: Specifically designed for R8 shrinking and inlining. Multi-scale fusion targets R8's method inlining optimization explicitly. Exact metrics not publicly verifiable.
papers.lib_level_f1: Exceeds single-scale baselines (exact metric unverified — full paper not publicly available)
papers.version_level_f1: Not publicly verifiable — claims exceed single-scale approaches
papers.partial_lib_handling: LDG construction inherently handles partial inclusion via dependency graph connectivity (library classes identified by their dependency relationships, not by complete inclusion)
papers.sbom_output: Yes — explicit SBOM generation is the primary goal of the tool. Pipeline: detection → SBOM → CVE mapping. Format not specified (likely CycloneDX or SPDX given focus on standardization).
papers.cve_mapping: Yes — SBOM + CVE mapping pipeline included
papers.transitive_deps: LDG (Library Dependency Graph) concept addresses transitive dependency representation — libraries linked to their sub-dependencies in the graph
strengths: Only tool with explicit SBOM generation as primary design goal — aligns perfectly with project objective
Multi-scale fusion (3 dependency graph levels) is the most robust architecture for R8-resilient detection
Bayesian probability scoring for version disambiguation is a key technique for adjacent-version accuracy
LDG concept enables transitive dependency representation — unique among all reviewed tools
weaknesses: Not publicly released — cannot be directly used or forked
Exact F1 scores and performance metrics unverifiable — paper lacks detailed quantitative results
Speed metrics not reported — unclear if multi-scale fusion introduces computational overhead
SBOM output format unspecified
papers.impact_on_project: CRITICAL — most project-relevant tool among all 10 papers reviewed. LibMD is the only tool that shares our exact goal: generating SBOMs from compiled Android APKs with CVE mapping. The multi-scale fusion architecture (class deps + method calls + basic block deps) is the most promising architecture for our MVP — providing redundancy against R8 optimizations by fusing information across dependency granularities. The Bayesian scoring for version disambiguation provides a mathematical framework we can adopt. The LDG concept opens the door for transitive dependency resolution, which no other tool addresses. Key gaps to fill in our implementation: (1) we need to specify a concrete SBOM format (CycloneDX recommended); (2) we need to validate speed; (3) we need to make our solution open source.

papers.title: A Systematic Assessment on Android Third-party Library Detection Tools
papers.detection_method: Systematic empirical evaluation of 9+ tools across 6 evaluation criteria. Extended version of ASE 2020 with 2 new metrics and 3 additional tools (LibExtractor, LibRoad, OSSPoLICE).
papers.module_decoupling: Evaluates 3 approaches: package-structure-based (error-prone — recommended against), CDG-based (recommended), signature-based. Confirms CDG is the superior approach.
papers.obfuscation_handling: Evaluated across RN, PF, CFR, DCR. CDG-based tools most resilient. Package-structure tools fail under RN. Signature tools fail under all obfuscation types.
papers.r8_resilience: Not explicitly tested (pre-dates R8 dominance). DCR (DexGuard) tested as closest proxy. Confirms CDG resilience to renaming-based obfuscation, which R8 uses aggressively.
papers.lib_level_f1: Varies by tool: LibScout best overall Gen-1
papers.version_level_f1: Most tools evaluated before version-level detection became standard — limited version metrics
papers.precision: Varies by tool — comprehensive comparison tables in paper
papers.recall: Varies by tool — most tools found to have low recall due to ignoring TPL dependencies and compilation mechanisms
papers.speed: LibRadar fastest. ORLIS crashes on apps requiring 16GB+ RAM.
papers.dataset_size: C1: apps with challenging TPL construction cases. C2: 221 apps + 59 TPLs with 2,115 versions. C4: two datasets (large code diff versions, small diff versions).
papers.partial_lib_handling: Evaluated — most tools fail to handle partial library inclusion correctly
papers.sbom_output: No tool produces standard SBOM format (confirmed as gap in the field)
papers.cve_mapping: Evaluated — most tools lack CVE mapping capability
papers.transitive_deps: Identified as key gap — most tools ignore TPL dependencies, contributing to low recall
strengths: Comprehensive 6-criteria evaluation framework (C1-C6) that can serve as our benchmarking standard
Identified concrete patches: multidex loop fix, .aar pre-processing, EntryPoint root detection
Empirically confirmed CDG-based module decoupling outperforms package-structure-based
Extended version covers 9+ tools providing the most complete comparative analysis in the literature
weaknesses: Pre-dates R8 — obfuscation evaluation does not cover R8 method inlining
Most tools evaluated have low recall due to unhandled edge cases
No tool evaluated produces standard SBOM output — confirms field-wide gap
Version-level detection was not standard at time of publication — limited version metrics
papers.impact_on_project: Foundational reference for benchmarking methodology. The 6-criteria framework (module decoupling accuracy, effectiveness, efficiency, version identification, obfuscation resilience, ease of use) directly maps to our evaluation needs. The empirical confirmation that CDG-based decoupling outperforms package-structure-based approaches validates our architectural direction. Three concrete implementation-level insights: (1) multidex APKs need special loop handling; (2) .aar format requires pre-processing; (3) EntryPoint root detection improves module boundary accuracy. The finding that most tools have low recall due to ignoring TPL dependencies reinforces the need for transitive dependency resolution in our MVP.

papers.title: Empirical Study of Third-Party Library Detection in iOS and Android Applications
papers.detection_method: Comprehensive empirical comparison of 7 Android TPL detection tools and 6 iOS TPL detection tools. F-Droid used for Android ground truth (open-source apps enable 100% verification). Manual download for iOS.
papers.module_decoupling: Evaluates tools using various methods: package-structure (LibRadar), signature-based (LibScout), CDG-based (LibID, LIBLOOM, ORLIS).
papers.matching_algorithm: N/A — evaluates multiple tools' algorithms across platforms
papers.obfuscation_handling: Android tools generally handle RN. iOS detection drops to 0% with symbol stripping (no iOS tool handles this).
papers.r8_resilience: Not explicitly tested — Android obfuscation coverage limited to RN evaluation
papers.lib_level_f1: LibScout most accurate for Android (highest F1 across evaluated tools)
papers.version_level_f1: Only LibScout could reliably identify versions on Android. iOS has ZERO version identification capability across all evaluated tools.
papers.precision: Evaluated per tool — LibScout highest precision for Android
papers.speed: LibRadar fastest among Android tools. ORLIS crashes on large apps (16GB+ RAM requirement)
papers.dataset_size: F-Droid Android apps (open-source, ground-truth verified). iOS apps manually downloaded.
papers.sbom_output: No tool produces SBOM output (confirmed across both platforms)
papers.cve_mapping: Android has far more CVEs detected than iOS. iOS CVE mapping essentially absent.
strengths: F-Droid methodology enables 100% ground truth verification — gold standard for Android evaluation
Comprehensive cross-platform comparison (Android + iOS) with 13 total tools evaluated
Confirms Android tooling is significantly more mature than iOS (10+ year gap)
Provides clear hybrid pipeline recommendation for practical deployments
weaknesses: Master's thesis — may have less rigorous methodology than peer-reviewed publications
Obfuscation evaluation limited to RN only — does not cover R8, DCR, or MI
Version-level detection evaluation limited — only LibScout evaluated for version accuracy
SBOM output gap confirmed but not explored in depth
papers.impact_on_project: Confirms Android-first focus is correct — iOS detection is approximately 10 years behind Android in TPL detection maturity, with zero version identification capability. The F-Droid validation methodology confirms this is the correct dataset for our ground truth evaluation. The hybrid pipeline recommendation (LibRadar for fast scan → LibScout/SAD for deep verification) validates our multi-stage architectural approach. The finding that Android has significantly more CVE detection capability reinforces the value proposition of our Android-focused SBOM generation tool.

critical_insights.unified_pipeline_synthesis: Across papers 6-10, a clear architectural pattern emerges: all top-performing tools use CDG-based module decoupling (confirmed by Papers 7, 8, 9) with a multi-stage verification pipeline (Papers 6, 10). LibMD (Paper 8) extends this to multi-scale fusion across 3 dependency graph levels — the most robust approach for R8-resilient detection.
critical_insights.key_gap: No tool (across all 5 papers) produces standard SBOM format output. LibMD (Paper 8) is the only tool that targets SBOM generation as a primary goal. This confirms our project fills a genuine gap.
critical_insights.r8_resilience_status: SAD (Paper 7) reports −10pp under MI (method inlining/R8 optimization). ATVHUNTER (Paper 6) not tested. LibMD (Paper 8) claims R8 resilience but metrics unverifiable. This remains the single hardest technical challenge.
critical_insights.benchmark_to_beat: Lib-level F1: 97.64% (SAD). Version-level F1: 88.8% (ATVHUNTER). Class-level F1: 94.12% (SAD). These are the current SOTA metrics our MVP must target.
critical_insights.recommended_architecture: CDG-based module decoupling + multi-scale dependency fusion (class, method, basic block) + Bayesian version disambiguation + CycloneDX SBOM + NVD/OSV CVE mapping + transitive dependency resolution via LDG concept.
